authority.legal_name: Maharashtra Maritime Board (MMB), the State maritime authority
authority.home_waters_label: Mumbai harbour, Thane creek and the Alibaug coast

mandate.summary: The Maharashtra Maritime Board is the State authority for ports and water transport in Maharashtra, developing Mumbai's passenger water-transport network — the Gateway–Mandwa RoPax, the Belapur water taxi, Elephanta and historic harbour ferries, plus a planned Mumbai water-metro — to relieve one of the world's most congested cities.
current_priorities: Developing Mumbai passenger water transport and jetties
Water-taxi and RoPax links across the harbour and to Navi Mumbai
Relieving extreme road congestion with clean water transport

policy_targets.vision: Maharashtra Maritime Board water-transport plan / Mumbai water metro
policy_targets.decarb_note: Mumbai's harbour ferries and the new water taxis still run on diesel, even as the MMB pushes new passenger water transport to relieve the city's gridlock — leaving a clear opening for zero-emission vessels.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission foiling layer for the network the Maharashtra Maritime Board is already building out — turning multi-hour road commutes between South Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and the Alibaug coast into fast, clean water lines.

precedent.headline: Public harbour ferries and water taxis are core Mumbai transport, not a novelty.
precedent.network: The MMB and operators run the Gateway of India–Mandwa RoPax and passenger ferries, the Belapur–South Mumbai water taxi, the Elephanta Caves line and the historic Bhaucha Dhakka ferries — with a Mumbai water-metro of dozens of terminals planned.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission foiling layer for the network the Maharashtra Maritime Board is already building out — turning multi-hour road commutes between South Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and the Alibaug coast into fast, clean water lines.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The flagship RoPax / passenger line across the harbour to Mandwa (Alibaug).
Historic Bhaucha Dhakka line to Mora (Uran).
Navi Mumbai water-taxi line to South Mumbai.
Harbour line to the Nhava Sheva port / industrial area.
Southern harbour line to Rewas / Alibaug.
Proposed west-coast water-metro line linking Bandra to South Mumbai.
Hub-spoke: Gateway of India ↔ Worli (orphan BP on published network)

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across Mumbai harbour, Thane creek and the Alibaug coast. Konkan-coast links (Ratnagiri etc.) are secondary and out of scope for this phase.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: Mumbai harbour is a major commercial and naval port (JNPT, Naval Dockyard) — routing must respect the shipping channel and naval exclusion zones; cross at marked points.
Thane creek is shallow with mangroves and is a protected flamingo habitat — follow the marked channel and keep low-wake clear of the mangroves.
The open harbour and Mandwa/Rewas crossings get rough in the southwest monsoon — flag seasonal limits; Quanta-LR for the more exposed legs.
The Atal Setu (MTHL) sea bridge and other piers cross the harbour — hand-waypoint clear of the pier protection zones.
